findings.description: The reports_archive bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects are stored with S3 default encryption (SSE-S3) rather than a customer-managed KMS key, and the vendor-roster seed object is uploaded without encryption settings.
No logging or access-logging configuration is present on the reports bucket, so access to the uploaded vendor roster and any other objects is not recorded for audit or incident response.
The ledger_exports bucket stores financial ledger data but has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving objects encrypted only with S3 default keys rather than a customer-managed KMS key.
The ledger bucket has no logging configuration, so reads and writes of sensitive financial exports are not logged.
The model_artifacts bucket has versioning and logging but no server_side_encryption_configuration, so model artifacts are not encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with any of these buckets, so a future ACL or policy change could expose the buckets publicly without a guardrail.
The ops_runbooks bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block; runbook content may include operational secrets and is not encrypted with a customer-managed key.
The runbooks bucket does not enable access logging, so requests for potentially sensitive operational documentation are not recorded.

The audit bucket is configured with acl = "log-delivery-write", which grants the S3 log delivery group write access to the bucket. Combined with the bucket being the logging target, this broadens write access beyond the intended principals and is not needed when using bucket policies instead of ACL-based log delivery.
The audit log bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so there is no account-level guardrail preventing public ACLs or policies on the bucket that holds security logs.

The vendor-roster.xlsx object is uploaded to the reports bucket with no kms_key_id or server-side encryption settings, so a spreadsheet containing vendor data is stored without customer-managed encryption.
